extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publishers, and research-integrity professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A news-summary page collecting articles about Hindawi/Wiley publishing problems; highlights standards, failures, and indicators used to evaluate journals and papers (peer review adequacy, citation integrity, image/text duplication, paper‑mill signals, retraction practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarivate’s quality criteria include ‘adequate peer review’ as a standard for inclusion in Web of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes journals can be delisted for failing to meet this criterion; failures cited include ‘compromised peer review’ and manipulated review processes that led publishers (Hindawi/Wiley) to retract many papers and close special-issue workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarivate’s quality criteria list ‘appropriate citations’ as a requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site gives examples of citation manipulation and suspicious citation patterns (e.g., thousands of ‘invisible citations’ inflating metrics, downloads vs citations mismatches flagged by tools) as reasons a title may fail this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content relevant to the stated scope of the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarivate’s quality criteria require content that’s ‘relevant to the stated scope of the journal.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarivate used this among 24 quality checks when removing titles; journals publishing out‑of‑scope or irrelevant material risk delisting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific reliability of articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction notices may cite ‘concerns about the article’s scientific reliability’ as grounds for retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include papers whose figures or data (e.g., fabricated or nonsensical error bars) undermine trust in the results; scientific reliability is a standard publishers use when deciding to retract.

rubrics_metrics.name: No duplicated or identical figures/images
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should not contain duplicated images or figures identical to those in other publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page recounts a case where multiple figures in a 2021 paper ‘look identical to figures in a 2019 paper’ (the earlier paper had been retracted), and such duplication was flagged on PubPeer as evidence of a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: No plagiarism / stolen text
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted articles must not appropriate text from others (plagiarism) or publish stolen work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a published article that reproduced part of a doctoral thesis word-for-word led to retraction and author disputes; plagiarism is an explicit cause for retraction and refund demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of the peer-review process (no manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals must avoid ‘compromised peer review’ and manipulated review workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents cases of manipulated or compromised peer review (e.g., special issues with compromised articles), and notes publishers identifying and retracting hundreds to thousands of papers where review integrity was breached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of paper-mill indicators (e.g., ‘tortured phrases’)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts and special issues should be free from paper-mill signals such as ‘tortured phrases’ and other text patterns suggesting automated or fraudulent production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Problematic Paper Screener flagged papers with ‘tortured phrases’; such linguistic anomalies, combined with other signals, have led to retraction and journal closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and timeliness of correction/retraction notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should publish timely, transparent notices when problems are reported or confirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page criticizes a former Hindawi journal for not publishing any notice 19 months after sleuths reported duplicated images, implying that delayed or absent notices are a failure of editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper editorial oversight and verification for special issues/guest editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Special-issue processes require appropriate oversight, including verification of guest-editor identities and editorial control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An example described where a professor used another person’s identity/email to edit special issues, contributing to compromised articles and eventual journal closures; stronger oversight is implied as a standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate and honest data/figure presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and graphical elements must accurately represent data (e.g., error bars should truly represent statistical uncertainty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes a paper whose error bars were actually capital ‘T’s pasted in, an indicator of fabrication or careless representation that justified retraction for undermining scientific reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of screening tools/algorithms to detect outlier characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexers and publishers may use AI or automated screening tools to identify outlier characteristics indicative of quality problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarivate developed an AI tool to flag outlier characteristics suggesting a journal may not meet quality criteria (it initially flagged >500 journals), and the page discusses automated screeners (Problematic Paper Screener) that helped identify suspect papers.
